items.title: The recorded search returned no records
items.whyItMatters: Nothing was retrieved or inspected, so no external estimate can guide the choice and no certainty can be claimed.
items.opportunity: Rerun a broader search before the design is revisited; meanwhile rely only on local data.

items.title: Completeness of INR records is unknown
items.whyItMatters: Time in range cannot be calculated where INRs are missing or entered late; a records comparison might measure data entry rather than dosing.
items.opportunity: Profile INR and dose records at all three clinics for four weeks before choosing a design.

items.title: Dosing approach is confounded with site
items.whyItMatters: Every nomogram patient is at the main site and every tool patient at a satellite, so adjustment can only use recorded case-mix variables.
items.opportunity: Record age, indication, interacting medicines and time on warfarin in the profile, whichever design follows.

items.title: Home-testing patients may be missing from the data
items.whyItMatters: Older patients, rural patients and patients with limited English who test at home are the most likely to have late or missing entries.
items.opportunity: Report completeness by testing mode and language, and do not exclude them silently.

items.title: Bleeding and clot events are too rare at clinic scale
items.whyItMatters: A clinic of 1,150 patients cannot show a difference in major events within a year.
items.opportunity: Use time in range as the primary outcome and report major events descriptively.

errorsFound: The first scan reply assigned a certainty and claimed the empty search was confirmed although no record was retrieved; both were dropped and the investigator confirmed the empty search on screen.
reevaluation: The gaps point to profiling the records before choosing between a records comparison and a randomised comparison.
summary: Five gaps; the empty search, unknown record completeness and site confounding are high severity.
